description: Make rauf a first-class agent-drivable tool: fix two log-integrity bugs that undermine programmatic consumption, refresh model guidance to tier aliases with 1M-context distinction, polish the web dashboard (config-root guard, ralph purge, favicon), formalize the machine-observation surfaces (NDJSON events + status --json) as a versioned contract, and add a pause-on-needs-human + resume-with-answer capability for live supervision. Source: plans/create-a-plan-to-compressed-oasis.md and ../feature-forge/plans/rauf-enhancement-recommendations.md.

items.title: Fix needsHuman log-pattern regex to match the runner's '(set aside)' line
items.description: The runner writes the needs-human log line as `Item <id> needs human input (set aside): <reason>` (packages/loop/src/runner.ts:699), but `LOG_PATTERNS.needsHuman` in packages/core/src/schemas.ts (around line 333) is `/Item \S+ needs human input: (.+)/`, which does NOT match because of the literal ` (set aside)` segment before the colon. As a result rauf's own log-derived status (and any log-fallback consumer) silently misses needs-human events. Fix: widen the regex to tolerate the optional segment, e.g. `/Item \S+ needs human input(?: \(set aside\))?: (.+)/`, keeping the single capture group returning just the reason. Do NOT change the emitted string in runner.ts — align the regex to the real output. Extend the LOG_PATTERNS test (packages/core/src/schemas.test.ts or wherever LOG_PATTERNS is tested) to assert both forms.
acceptanceCriteria: LOG_PATTERNS.needsHuman matches `Item 007 needs human input (set aside): db migration unclear` and captures `db migration unclear`
The regex still matches the legacy `Item 007 needs human input: reason` form
A test in packages/core asserts both the (set aside) and legacy forms match and capture the reason
Verification passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Confirmed bug. The capture must return only the reason, not the `(set aside)` text. Source: feature-forge handoff §4.

items.title: Redact RAUF_* tokens in the Signal-text log dump
items.description: When a claude iteration exits with no parsed terminal signal, the runner appends a diagnostic `Signal text (source=<src>, len=<n>):\n<preview>` line to rauf.log, where preview is up to the last 500 chars of raw agent stdout (packages/loop/src/runner.ts:614-618). Agent prose can contain a literal RAUF_DONE / RAUF_BLOCKED / RAUF_NEEDS_HUMAN token, which then false-matches any consumer (or human) grepping rauf.log for terminal signals. Fix: sanitize the preview before logging so the three terminal tokens are no longer literal-token matches — e.g. replace RAUF_DONE -> RAUF·DONE (middle dot) or wrap as ⟨RAUF_DONE⟩, for all three tokens. Keep the `source=` and `len=` diagnostics and the rest of the preview readable. Prefer extracting a small pure helper (e.g. redactSignalTokens(text): string) so it is unit-testable. Add a test (packages/loop/src/runner.test.ts or a focused helper test) asserting a preview containing `... RAUF_DONE ...` in prose is redacted in the appended log line so a token grep no longer matches.
acceptanceCriteria: The Signal-text preview redacts RAUF_DONE / RAUF_BLOCKED / RAUF_NEEDS_HUMAN so they are not literal-token matches in rauf.log
The `source=` and `len=` diagnostics are preserved
A test asserts redaction of a terminal token embedded in agent prose
Verification passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Confirmed. rauf.log is a human surface, but this also protects rauf's own log-derived parsing and any log-fallback consumer. Source: feature-forge handoff §5.

items.title: Refresh model guidance to tier aliases + document opus[1m] for 1M items
items.description: Replace stale pinned model ids with tier aliases and add 1M-context guidance. items.notes: 1M is strictly opt-in via the `[1m]` suffix on aliases or full ids; Opus 1M has no cost premium. Authoritative source: claude --help + code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config. Source: feature-forge handoff §6.

items.title: Add config-root product guard (specific dashboard message + Settings validation)
items.description: When the configured rootDirectory does not exist, discoverProjects returns a clear error `Root directory does not exist: <path>` (packages/core/src/discovery.ts:28-47), but the web dashboard renders it as a generic "Failed to load projects" and the Settings page does no validation. (1) Dashboard: in the error branch of packages/web/src/client/routes/projects/index.tsx, detect the root-not-found error (by the code/message from the /api/projects 500 response) and show a targeted message naming the path — e.g. "Root directory `<path>` does not exist — set it in Settings." with a link to /settings — instead of the generic box. (2) Settings: in packages/web/src/client/routes/settings.tsx, add pre-save validation of the entered rootDirectory — warn (and/or block save) with a clear message when the path doesn't exist. The server already knows existence via discovery; reuse the existing discovery error, or add a small read-only endpoint (e.g. GET /api/settings/validate-root?path=...) under packages/web/src/server/routes that stat-checks the path and returns { exists: boolean }. Keep any new endpoint read-only and path-sandboxed consistently with existing routes (127.0.0.1 only; X-Rauf-Request header rules apply to mutations, not this GET).
acceptanceCriteria: A nonexistent rootDirectory yields a specific dashboard message naming the path plus a Settings link (not the generic "Failed to load projects")
The Settings page warns when the entered rootDirectory does not exist, before/at save
Any new endpoint is read-only and validates/sandboxes its input
Verification passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: The local ~/.rauf/config.json value itself is fixed manually outside this item; this is the in-product guard so future bad-root cases are clear.

items.title: Document NDJSON events + status --json as a versioned machine contract
items.description: Elevate rauf's machine-observation surfaces to a documented, versioned contract. In docs/SPEC-BACKLOG-TOOL-CONTRACT.md (Part A is the STABLE contract: sections A.1–A.6, A.5 = versioning), add a new Part-A section (e.g. A.7 "Machine-observation surfaces (versioned)") documenting, as a promise downstream supervisors may rely on: (1) the `loop run … --ndjson` event vocabulary — the LoopEvent `type` set and base fields { type, timestamp, projectPath } (packages/core/src/schemas.ts:552-576 and :404-407), with payloads for the consumer-critical events item_completed, item_blocked, needs_human, signal_parsed, loop_completed, loop_error, loop_cancelled, llm_stuck_warning; and the two gotchas EXPLICITLY: signal_parsed.signal collapses review->done (runner.ts:607), and a circuit-breaker halt is emitted as loop_error (no distinct circuit_breaker type, runner.ts:1173). State an additive-only / versioned compatibility promise anchored to A.5. (2) `status … --json` DerivedStatus (schemas.ts:263-276) as the canonical status surface — loopState enum, backlogSummary fields (and that blocked vs needsHuman vs deferred are distinct), lock, and the exit-code table (RUNNING->1, PAUSED_HUMAN->2, LIMIT_REACHED->3, else 0). (3) The machine-vs-human distinction: --ndjson and status --json are MACHINE surfaces; `loop follow`, `log --follow`, and rauf.log are HUMAN-formatted and must not be parsed programmatically. Cross-reference from docs/SPEC-CLI.md (the --ndjson / status --json verbs) and docs/SCHEMAS.md (which holds the shapes) to this new section as the source of truth; keep the shapes in SCHEMAS, the promise here. Event/field/enum names must match schemas.ts exactly.
acceptanceCriteria: SPEC-BACKLOG-TOOL-CONTRACT.md has a new Part-A section documenting the NDJSON event vocabulary (with the review->done and circuit-breaker->loop_error gotchas), DerivedStatus + the exit-code table, and the machine-vs-human surface rule
Event/field/enum names in the doc match packages/core/src/schemas.ts exactly
docs/SPEC-CLI.md and docs/SCHEMAS.md cross-reference the new section
Docs build clean: `bash scripts/setup-docs.sh && pnpm --filter @rauf/docs build`, and `git status` is clean after the build
Verification passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Pure docs. These surfaces already exist; this makes them a contract feature-forge can rely on. Source: feature-forge handoff §1, §2, §5-docs.

items.title: Add `loop run --pause-on-needs-human` halt mode (+ loop_paused event + exit code)
items.description: Add an opt-in run mode that halts the loop when an item emits RAUF_NEEDS_HUMAN, so a supervising session can detect the pause. Default behavior MUST be unchanged (today the runner sets the item aside as blocked+needsHuman and keeps running — packages/loop/src/runner.ts:679-701). Steps: (1) Add a `--pause-on-needs-human` boolean flag to `rauf loop run`; thread it through handleLoopRun + LoopStartOptions (packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts) into LoopRunner options. (2) In the needs_human handler (runner.ts:679-701): when the flag is set, after setting the item aside, HALT — modeled on haltForUsageLimit (runner.ts:1186-1196): writeState("paused_human", null) (clear currentItem), write the pause/DONE marker, and return "exit" so the loop stops; when the flag is off, keep today's behavior. (3) Add a new LoopEvent `loop_paused { reason: "needs_human", itemId }` to the discriminated union in packages/core/src/schemas.ts AND to the --ndjson subscription list in loop-commands.ts; emit the existing needs_human event then loop_paused at the halt. (4) Add a distinct non-zero exit code for "halted for human input" to the ExitCode map (packages/cli/src/commands.ts:91-98) and return it from handleLoopRun when the loop halts in paused_human (status already exits 2 for PAUSED_HUMAN). Add unit tests for the pause-vs-keep-going branch, the loop_paused emission, and the exit code.
acceptanceCriteria: `loop run --pause-on-needs-human` halts in state paused_human on the first needs-human item; WITHOUT the flag, behavior is unchanged (loop keeps running other items)
A `loop_paused {reason:"needs_human", itemId}` NDJSON event is emitted at the halt; the needs_human event is still emitted
handleLoopRun returns a distinct non-zero exit code on a needs-human halt
Unit tests cover the branch, the loop_paused event, and the exit code
Verification passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Template = haltForUsageLimit (runner.ts:1186-1196). paused_human already in the state enum (schemas.ts:165) and maps to status exit 2. Document loop_paused/flag/exit-code in item 010. Source: feature-forge handoff §3.

items.title: Add `resume --answer <id> "<text>"` injecting the answer into the item
items.description: Let a supervisor inject a human's answer into a paused item and resume it. Builds on item 008's paused_human halt. Steps: (1) Extend BacklogItemSchema (packages/core/src/schemas.ts:33-67) with optional `humanAnswer?: string`; if schemas/backlog.schema.json is generated from zod, regenerate via pnpm generate:schemas. (2) Add "paused_human" to RESUMABLE_RAW_STATUSES (packages/cli/src/resume-commands.ts:129-136). (3) Add a repeatable `--answer <itemId> "<text>"` option to `rauf resume` (handleResume, ~200-372). Before the reconcile/recover step, for each answer pair call updateItem(itemId, { humanAnswer: <text>, status: "pending", needsHuman: false, blockedReason: null }) so the item re-queues to pending with its answer attached. (4) Thread the answer into the prompt: in buildPrompt (packages/loop/src/prompt-builder.ts:147-244) add a section immediately AFTER the "Your Current Task" section and BEFORE the backlog summary: `## Human's Answer to Your Previous Question\n\n<humanAnswer>` — only when item.humanAnswer is set. (5) Auto-clear humanAnswer when the item completes (in the item_completed path in runner.ts where updateItem sets status done) so a later unrelated retry never re-injects a stale answer. Add unit tests for --answer parsing + item mutation, the prompt-builder section presence/absence, and auto-clear on completion.
acceptanceCriteria: `rauf resume . --answer 003 "use schema v5"` re-queues item 003 to pending with humanAnswer set and needsHuman cleared
buildPrompt includes the "Human's Answer" section iff item.humanAnswer is set, positioned after the task and before the backlog summary
humanAnswer is cleared when the item completes
Unit tests cover --answer parsing, the item mutation, the prompt section, and auto-clear
Verification passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Answer-persistence semantics: clear-on-done (not a history field). resume is generic over RESUMABLE_RAW_STATUSES; --answer mutation happens before reconcile/recover. Source: feature-forge handoff §3.

items.title: End-to-end sandbox scenario + docs for pause/resume-on-needs-human
items.description: Add an end-to-end test-sandbox scenario for pause->resume-with-answer, and document the new surfaces. (1) test-sandbox: add a scenario where the mock claude script emits RAUF_NEEDS_HUMAN for an item (see test-sandbox/README.md for how scenarios + mock-claude work). Assert that `rauf loop run <sandbox> --pause-on-needs-human` halts in state paused_human, emits needs_human + loop_paused on the --ndjson stream, and exits the distinct needs-human exit code; then `rauf resume <sandbox> --answer <id> "answer"` re-queues the item, the next iteration's prompt contains the "Human's Answer" section, the item completes, and humanAnswer is cleared. Wire it into test-sandbox/verify.sh so `bash test-sandbox/verify.sh` exercises it. (2) Docs: document the `--pause-on-needs-human` flag and the `resume --answer` verb in docs/SPEC-CLI.md, and add the loop_paused event + the new exit code to the Part-A machine-surface contract section created in item 007. Note the supervisor pattern: run with `--ndjson --pause-on-needs-human`; on loop_paused/needs_human, gather an answer, call `resume --answer`.
acceptanceCriteria: A new test-sandbox scenario exercises the pause (paused_human + loop_paused + the new exit code) then resume --answer (re-queue, answer-in-prompt, completion, humanAnswer cleared)
`bash test-sandbox/verify.sh` runs the new scenario and passes
docs/SPEC-CLI.md documents --pause-on-needs-human and resume --answer; the Part-A contract section documents the loop_paused event and the new exit code
Verification passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check (and docs build clean)
